best_for: Notion and Miro users who want notes, databases and a whiteboard in one app, with their files kept on their own disk or on a server they run.
description:
AFFiNE is a workspace for notes, wikis and planning, built in the open on GitHub by the team at toeverything. Its makers say they took ideas from Notion's blocks, Trello's Kanban boards and Miro's whiteboards and put them in one app.

You can build a team wiki, plan a project, sketch a storyboard or a mood board, or map out ideas as a mind map. When you need to show your work, you frame parts of the canvas as slides and present them. Ready-made templates get you started, such as a digital planner, Cornell notes, a checklist and a travel itinerary. The optional AFFiNE AI can draft a report, turn an outline into slides or sum up an article as a mind map.

points.title: Docs and whiteboard are one space
points.text: Any page can switch to an edgeless canvas where text, sticky notes, shapes, embeds, databases and slides sit side by side.

points.title: Local first, cloud optional
points.text: Your workspace lives on your disk, and you can add real-time sync and sharing when you need it. The Community Edition is MIT licensed and can be self-hosted with Docker.

points.title: Free plan limits
points.text: The free cloud tier gives 10 GB of storage, files up to 10 MB, 3 members per workspace, 7 days of history and up to 3 signed-in devices.

points.title: Paid tiers
points.text: Pro is listed at USD 6.75 per month for 100 GB, 100 MB files, 10 members and 30 days of history. Team is USD 10 per seat per month billed yearly, and the AI add-on is USD 8.9 per month billed yearly. A one-time Believer plan is USD 499.99 with 1 TB. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Still filling in
points.text: Version numbers are still below 1.0. The README says plugins and third-party blocks are coming soon, and the Enterprise Edition with SSO and audit tools is not out yet.

points.title: Windows and Mac installs
points.text: Windows has x64 and Arm64 installers that install for the current user or for the whole machine. The Mac app has Intel and Apple silicon builds and needs macOS 12. Linux is not listed here.

points.title: Older versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 56 versions. macOS lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
